links.comparator_used: Conventional complaint-driven (reactive) surveillance, compared in a 12-month simulation with synthetic drift
links.outcome: Timing of detection of performance degradation (sensitivity decline)
links.effect: DARL detected degradation at month 5, when sensitivity had fallen only 2.5 percentage points from the 94.0% baseline. The DARL Risk Score crossed the High-risk trigger at month 10, before sensitivity reached its terminal 85.0%, an advance of about six weeks over reactive detection.
links.quote: A 12-month simulation study, conducted under controlled synthetic drift conditions based on published AI benchmarks, demonstrates that DARL detects early-stage performance degradation at month 5, when model sensitivity had declined by only 2.5 percentage points from the validated baseline of 94.0%, a point at which conventional complaint-driven surveillance systems would not generate a structured risk signal.

design_hint: continuous drift monitoring with threshold-based risk triggers
